title: Support Fastpath: Adaptive runlet fabric for instant admin actions
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Goal: Build 'Support Fastpath', a lightweight adaptive runlet fabric that converts approved runbook snippets into event-triggered micro-tasks (runlets) for rapid, audited operator actions. The feature targets first-response support flows: common triage steps, safe restarts, cache clears, and short-lived rollback operations.

Scope:
- Authoring: provide a small schema for runlet-safe inputs and parameter validation (typed strings, enums, secrets refs).
- Execution: event-triggered, single-step or small multi-step runlets with per-step RBAC and idempotency checks.
- Observability: emit step-level traces to Console, token-level cost estimate, and outcome metrics to the Ops dashboard.
- Safety: integrate permission gating, dry-run mode, and an automatic cooldown (circuit-breaker) on repeated failures.

Out of scope for this ticket: full visual runbook editor, long-running multi-step flows (>5 min), and offline orchestration. Those will be covered in a future follow-up.

Architecture notes:
- Runlets will be modeled as JSON manifests stored in the Admin Utility store (KVS). A small translate layer converts Linear/Confluence runbook snippets into runlet manifests (spike implemented in spike/support-fastpath/).
- Execution will reuse the existing runlet executor harness in ops-runner but with a thin shim that enforces sequence-level timeouts and KV cache isolation.
- Telemetry: leverage admin-telemetry pipeline (see ENG-642000) to tag traces with runlet_id, principal, and feature_flag.
- Rollout plan: opt-in via feature-flag for 10% of org (beta tenants), then expand with canary metrics in console-ops.

Why this is different: Instead of a full runbook-as-code system, Fastpath focuses on low-friction, high-confidence micro-actions that reduce mean time to remediation for common incidents without requiring heavy authoring or orchestration overhead.
acceptance_criteria: Authoring UI: Engineers can create a runlet manifest via the CLI or minimal web form and save to Admin Utility store with schema validation
Execution: A runlet can be executed from the Console and via REST API; each run emits a trace and a cost estimate in the Console
Safety: Runlet executions enforce RBAC and require either a user confirmation or an approved service token for automated triggers
Observability: All runlet executions appear in Ops dashboard with step-level duration, success/failure, and associated trace links
Rollout: Feature-flag gated rollout to a beta tenant group with telemetry confirming no regressions in latency or error-rate
